title: Cross-team leads sprint snapshot — 2026-07-08
content:
Date: 2026-07-08
Attendees: Aisha (host), Marco, Sofia, Daniel, Priya, Elena (serving-runtime), Ravi (observability), Mei (private-deploy), Tomas (dedicated infra), Erin (product-hosted-api)
Apologies: Omar (SRE)

Purpose: quick cross-team snapshot to align priorities for the sprint boundary week, raise immediate operational risks, and review a few rollout decisions that need leadership sign-off. Target duration 45 minutes; kept to ~50.

1) Quick wins / Notes since last week
- Serving-runtime: kernel selection changes for 2.2.1 landed in staging; microbenchmarks show 8–12% token cost reduction for opt-6.7b workloads when sequence length <1024. (Elena)
- Observability: added token-level cost breakdown in the route dashboard alpha — internal only. Sampling config default changed to 5% to avoid ingestion burst. (Ravi)
- Private: completed first on-prem install checklist with customer ACME Health (air-gapped pilot). Two issues in preflight: HSM cert rotation and outbound telemetry gating. (Mei)
- Dedicated: autoscaler tweak fixed a hot-shard degradation case — backfill still in progress. (Tomas)

2) Metrics / health headlines (top lines)
- P99 latency (hosted text generation, eu-west): 120ms (target 110ms). Regressed after last kernel rollout on 2026-07-02 for long-context workloads.
- Error rate (5xx) across hosted API: 0.3% last 24h (baseline 0.15%). Root cause trace points to a rate-limiter edge-case when prefix-cache misses spike.
- Capacity burn (Dedicated pool C): 86% commit utilization; projected overcommit risk in 96h if no extra nodes added.
- Cost delta: week-over-week token cost down 3% overall due to batching improvements in prod.

3) Blockers and escalations (needs triage / decisions)
- Blocker A: P99 regression followup
  - Summary: Long-context requests (L > 2048) hitting a slower kernel path; fallback to safe kernel increases CPU usage and P99. Elena proposes a targeted microscopic revert of the selector rule for L > 2048 while we iterate.
  - Impact: user-facing latency bump for a subset of customers (not all); can affect SLAs for a small set of enterprise tenants.
  - Decision requested: approve hotfix revert for eu-west and us-central canary, then run extended perf test. Owner: Elena. Due: 2026-07-09 EOD.

- Blocker B: Dedicated pool C capacity risk
  - Summary: Commit utilization projected to exceed committed capacity due to two new customers onboarding this week + an unexpectedly large burst test.
  - Asks: short term — approve burst nodes (non-reserved) for 72h; medium — accelerate node procurement (Tomas to own).
  - Cost/impact: temporary 18% cost increase for the affected pool if approved; prevents throttling and potential customer SLA breaches.

- Blocker C: Private deployment telemetry gating
  - Summary: ACME requires strict no-egress telemetry by default; current private installer uses an outbound health-check to telemetry.redwood.ai during install.
  - Proposal: make telemetry ping optional behind a flag and default to offline install mode. Mei to produce patch + test matrix. Target: 2026-07-15.

4) Cross-team project sync (brief)
- Canary rollouts / fallback policy (Product + SRE)
  - Product asks: add an automated fallback rule that will switch routes to a smaller model variant when P99 > threshold for 10 minutes. Implementation options: runtime-side policy vs. control-plane rule.
  - Consensus: prefer control-plane rule for visibility, but runtime should support fast switch. Action: Daniel + Erin to produce a short design doc by 2026-07-12. Link: JIRA:ENG-2187.

- Cost optimization experiment (Optimize team + Serving)
  - Running an A/B between quantized vq8 and q4f32 on midrange workloads. Early signal: 6% latency increase but 22% token cost reduction. Need quality evals on prompt suite. Action: Marco to coordinate eval set + summary by 2026-07-14.

- Observability retention change (Observability)
  - Proposed retention reduction for debug-level traces from 30d -> 14d to cut cost. Ravi to run risk assessment on incident post-mortem availability. Decision tentatively approved pending SRE input.

5) Action items (owner / due / status)
- Elena: roll hotfix revert for kernel selector for L>2048 to eu-west + us-central canary; run perf tests — due 2026-07-09 EOD — status: in_progress.
- Tomas: approve temporary burst nodes for Dedicated Pool C and start procurement ticket — due 2026-07-09 AM — status: open. Linked: JIRA:OPS-452.
- Mei: add offline-install flag and update installer docs; add test matrix for HSM rotation — due 2026-07-15 — status: open.
- Daniel & Erin: short design doc for automated route fallback (control-plane first) — due 2026-07-12 — status: assigned.
- Marco: assemble prompt-eval set for quantization A/B and run quality regressions — due 2026-07-14 — status: assigned.
- Ravi: retention risk assessment and proposed roll-back plan for trace TTL change — due 2026-07-13 — status: assigned.

6) Decisions made in meeting
- Approve hotfix revert for kernel selector in eu-west/us-central canaries (vote: unanimous).
- Approve temporary burst nodes for Pool C (leadership will absorb temporary overage) — conditional on procurement ticket by TOMAS today.
- Observability TTL reduction: proceed with pilot but do not change global defaults until post-pilot review.

7) Loose ends / parking lot
- Follow-up on enterprise SLA notification flow: when we hit a protected SLA, notification path should include on-call + account manager + platform lead. Action: Priya to draft a notification playbook by 2026-07-16.
- Long-term: evaluate kernel selector logic rewrite (this needs a multi-sprint plan). Put on engineering roadmap discussion next leadership sync.
- Hiring: platform infra IC hiring still slow — two offers extended; need help from recruiting to close.

8) Quick round-robin updates (1–2 bullets each)
- Product (Erin): launch checklist for new streaming feature almost ready; expect PRD freeze 2026-07-13.
- SRE (Omar, via note): investigating intermittent QPS spikes tied to a customer test harness. Correlation with dedicated pool bursts.
- Solutions Eng: ramping trial with major fintech customer; hitting private deployment preflight blockers (Mei owner).

9) Notes to self / meeting artifacts
- Recording: slack thread #leadership-weekly (link pinned) and meeting recording archived in Confluence under deployment-runbook-2026Q3.
- Next meeting: 2026-07-15 (same time). Proposal: shift to 40-minute strict cadence to reduce follow-up slippage.

Open questions (explicit):
- Do we want an explicit cost budget guardrail for burst nodes above 48h? (If yes, define threshold and approvers)
- How aggressively should we default to caching-focused suggestions in Optimize UI for new customers? (Marco to propose defaults)

End notes: informal fragments still in progress; will tidy and convert to final runbook if decisions land. If you want to add items, edit inline and ping owner.

-- Aisha
